entry.title: .NET 10 Release 1: Performance Boosts, Security Upgrades, and Smarter AI
entry.summary:
.NET 10 RC1 is here, and it's a monster. Think your code is fast now? Just wait. The team pulled a Frederic Tudor, the 19th-century "Ice King," compounding thousands of tiny optimizations into a massive performance leap. The JIT is now a wizard at "deabstraction," making your clean, high-level C# run like hand-tuned C.
The real magic trick? Expanded escape analysis. The compiler can now stack-allocate small objects that it proves don't "escape" a method. That means less heap allocation and fewer GC pauses. It's the free performance lunch you were always told doesn't exist. Your app gets faster without you changing a line of code.

entry.title: SQL Server Myth: “DBCC DROPCLEANBUFFERS / DBCC FREEPROCCACHE are harmless troubleshooting tools”
entry.summary:
DBCC DROPCLEANBUFFERS removes all clean data pages from the buffer pool. The next queries hit storage (disk/SSD) instead of memory.
DBCC FREEPROCCACHE removes all compiled plans from the plan cache. Queries across the whole instance must recompile, spiking CPU.

entry.title: System of Record And Source of Single Truth Are Not The Same
entry.summary: I recently blogged about the importance of distinct and isolated subsystems where real-time data transactions that apply to a particular business data entity are processed, known as a System of Record. Someone referenced that post and incorrectly implied that I was suggesting a Single Source of Truth. I didn't delve deeper into Single Source of Truth in that post to keep it concise. Still, I was careful to suggest "how important it is to separate operational systems from analytical systems" and that analytical systems "must support multiple independent Systems of Record." And in fact, I diagrammed information refinement and how it progresses within enterprises. That diagram isolated Systems of Record from a Single Source of Truth and isolated Operational Systems from Analytical Systems. In this post, I want to detail how and why a Single Source of Truth is different from Systems of Record.
